summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson, a male with a history of mixed Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma with CNS involvement, was admitted for maintenance high-dose methotrexate and rituximab chemotherapy. He remained asymptomatic throughout the stay but developed transient acute kidney injury with creatinine peaking at 1.9 mg/dL, likely methotrexate-induced, which improved to 1.5 mg/dL by discharge. Leucovorin was increased to 100 mg every six hours during the period of renal dysfunction. Mild transaminitis and hypokalemia were noted and managed supportively. Constipation was treated with a Fleet's enema and transition to Miralax. Omeprazole and aspirin were held during admission and restarted at discharge. Methotrexate levels declined appropriately, falling below 0.1 µM by discharge. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans for outpatient MRI and ophthalmology follow-up.
